item.title: Attractors and initial-condition sensitivity in Horndeski cosmologies
item.description: arXiv:2610.36036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study whether nearby homogeneous cosmological histories approach or move away from the Genesis and contracting solutions. We also determine how an uncertainty in the scalar velocity at a later stage affects the inferred initial velocity. In the Genesis models, including the gravitational dynamics can substantially change this relation. We find that convergence of homogeneous solutions can occur even around backgrounds with unstable perturbations, and therefore attraction of the background is not sufficient to establish that a cosmological solution is physically viable. In the contracting model, one power-law solution attracts nearby trajectories, whereas another repels them. The strength of these effects depends on how the cosmological state is parametrized. Their evolution through the subsequent bounce is not considered here.
item.dc:creator: Yulia A. Ageeva, Andrey K. Sharofeev

item.title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.08958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalise the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including general axial conditions that allow for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behaviour of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Matheus G. Barbosa

item.title: Efficiency enhancement in a two-detector Unruh quantum Otto engine
item.description: arXiv:2611.11917v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate efficiency enhancement in an Unruh quantum Otto engine (UQOE) consisting of two initially uncorrelated Unruh-DeWitt (UDW) detectors. The detectors undergo uniform acceleration with different magnitudes and couple locally to a massless scalar field prepared in the Minkowski vacuum. We choose a diagonal free Hamiltonian for the UQOE and define its work and heat with respect to the proper time of one of the detectors. Consequently, the coherence terms generated through the interaction with the scalar field do not directly contribute to the work and heat of the UQOE. Instead, the efficiency enhancement arises from the relative proper-time weighting of the detectors' local population changes. We identify operating points that satisfy the conditions of initial-state passivity, cycle closure, and energy conservation. The efficiency is higher than that of a conventional UQOE, and the state of the UQOE after the heat absorption stage is separable. We further investigate the influence of detector separation on cycle closure and efficiency. Although the local population responses are independent of separation at fixed control parameters, the nonlocal coherence terms depend on separation and impose additional constraints on state cycle closure. Restoring closure generally requires retuning the cycle parameters, which can indirectly modify the achievable efficiency enhancement. Our results demonstrate that, within the second-order perturbative framework and the adopted energy convention, entanglement generation is not necessary for efficiency enhancement. They also clarify the distinct roles of local population changes and nonlocal coherences in the thermodynamic operation of a two-detector UQOE.
item.dc:creator: Yongjie Pan, Baocheng Zhang, Qingyu Cai

item.title: Conserved Gravitational-wave Stress-Energy Tensor in General Metric Theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.15321v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a gravitational-wave (GW) stress-energy tensor for general metric theories and show that it is conserved after averaging in the wave zone. In metric theories involving a vector field, we find that the conventional GW stress-energy tensor is generally not conserved. Combining the diffeomorphism identity, we identify the vector-field contribution required in addition to the conventional GW stress-energy tensor. On this basis, in a flat vacuum wave zone with constant background fields and after short-wavelength averaging, the perturbed field equation, perturbed action, Landau-Lifshitz, and Noether current methods yield equivalent tensors. In this setting, the completed tensor is generally nonsymmetric and satisfies $\partial_\mu\tau^{\mu\nu}=0$, with energy flux $c\tau^{i0}$. It also does not depend on whether a covariant or contravariant vector is chosen as the fundamental variable. Applying this framework to Einstein-\ae ther theory, we derive the orbital energy losses of an adiabatic quasicircular compact binary, and provide a possible explanation for the discrepancies among previous results in this theory. These results establish a consistent radiation balance that allows additional gravitational degrees of freedom to be connected to the evolution of astrophysical systems and to observational tests of gravity.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Bin Lai, Yu-Zhi Fan, Yu-Qi Dong, Yu-Xiao Liu

item.title: Approximate Decoherence, Recoherence and Records in Isolated Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2601.19703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the framework of decoherent histories, we study which past events leave detectable records in isolated quantum systems under the realistic assumption that decoherence is approximate and not perfect. Using tools from quantum state discrimination, we establish asymptotically for a large class of (pseudo-)random histories how the strength of decoherence changes the number of reliable records, i.e., we quantitatively answer the question: when can approximate decoherence be approximated by exact decoherence? In addition, we reveal a clear decoherence structure for long histories based on a numerically exact solution of a random matrix model that, as we argue, captures generic aspects of decoherence. In particular, we observe strong recoherences for maverick histories that are statistical outliers with respect to Born's rule. From the perspective of the Many Worlds Interpretation, our results reveal a "branch selection problem" and shed light on the emergence of Born's rule and the theory confirmation problem.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Strasberg, Joseph Schindler, Jiaozi Wang, Andreas Winter

item.title: Magnetic Catalysis and Fermion Mass Generation in de Sitter Spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2608.07270v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the dynamics of a charged fermion in de Sitter space in the presence of a uniform background magnetic field, and discuss magnetic catalysis of chiral symmetry breaking using the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model. We evaluate the mode functions of the charged fermion field in this background by imposing the Bunch--Davies vacuum condition. The gap equation is solved in the mean-field approximation. We derive analytic expressions for the gap in several limiting regimes, such as the large-magnetic-field and large-curvature limits. We find that the curvature effect restores chiral symmetry, whereas the magnetic field enhances chiral symmetry breaking through the conventional mechanism of magnetic catalysis. The phase structure associated with chiral symmetry breaking is revealed by numerical calculations.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Fujikura, Toshifumi Noumi, Shintetsu Yamazaki

item.title: Modular flow and the area operator
item.description: arXiv:2609.14165v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, the Jafferis-Lewkowycz-Maldacena-Suh (JLMS) formula relates the boundary modular Hamiltonian to the HRT area operator and the corresponding bulk modular Hamiltonian. In standard discussions of a holographic code built from perturbative excitations on a fixed classical background, the $A/4G$ term dominates over the bulk modular Hamiltonian in the limit $G \to 0$. However, this setup is insufficient to describe the action of boundary modular flows that change the classical background. In contrast, our recent discussion of `large' codes provides a useful framework to obtain a JLMS formula that relates bulk and boundary modular flows acting on appropriate states in the code. Here, one sees that the bulk modular Hamiltonian is not in fact subdominant when the modular flow defined by one state acts on another state peaked around a sufficiently different classical background. Instead, the bulk modular Hamiltonian can be of order $1/G$ and can dominate over the $A/4G$ term. Nevertheless, we show that if the two states have the same classical background except for data conjugate to the HRT area then, under mild assumptions and over a large range of flow parameters, the modular-flowed state is described by a classical background given by the HRT-area flow alone.
item.dc:creator: Xi Dong, Donald Marolf, Pratik Rath

item.title: Black Hole Entropy and Holographic Entanglement Entropy in DGP Brane Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.05946v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the relation between gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy in braneworld gravity with gravitational dynamics localized on the brane. We first consider the DGP brane model, in which an Einstein-Hilbert term is included in the brane action, and demonstrate that the gravitational entropy of a braneworld black hole agrees with the holographic entanglement entropy for general stationary spacetimes. We then generalize the brane-localized Einstein-Hilbert term to higher-curvature gravitational theories. For Lovelock gravity and $f(R)$ gravity on the brane, we derive the corresponding expressions for gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy and show that the two entropies also coincide for general stationary spacetimes. These results establish the equivalence between gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy in braneworld gravity for a broad class of gravitational theories and contribute to a deeper understanding of holography in braneworld settings.
item.dc:creator: Takamasa Kanai

item.title: Graviphoton mixing with KK modes in the 2D effective theory of charged black holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29068v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the effects of massive Kaluza--Klein modes on the two-dimensional low-energy effective theory obtained by the $S^2$ reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory on a Reissner--Nordstr\"om black hole background. We retain the first excited ($l=1$) Maxwell Kaluza--Klein modes in addition to the massless sector. The background electric flux mixes the Maxwell Kaluza--Klein scalars with the graviphotons, and tree-level exchange of the massive scalars generates a correction to the graviphoton kinetic term proportional to the square of the black hole charge. Within the leading local approximation, we also perturbatively evaluate the one-loop correction to the graviphoton kinetic term and find no dependence on the black hole charge. We find that near extremality, the charge-dependent tree-level correction becomes parametrically comparable to the classical graviphoton kinetic term.
item.dc:creator: Yoshihiko Abe, Tetsutaro Higaki, Yu Miyauchi

item.title: Imaging the two-sided black hole interior with four-point correlators
item.description: arXiv:2611.15933v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a boundary four-point function smeared with wavepackets, which probes local physics behind the horizon of a two-sided AdS black hole. At high frequencies, boundary wavepackets aimed at an interior bulk point travel along geodesics and scatter locally about the bulk point, factorizing the correlator into a flat-space like scattering amplitude. To obtain this configuration, we utilize a non-trivial time ordering of operators, and also use one state-dependent operator insertion moved halfway across the thermal circle. An interesting property of this observable is that it also probes features of nontrivial states: null shocks and matter shells behind the horizon show up as jumps in the observed signal as the bulk point crosses them, thereby imaging the black hole interior.
item.dc:creator: Joydeep Chakravarty
